title: Convergence Dynamics of Over-Parameterized Score Matching for a Single Gaussian
claim: Over-parameterized training shows two distinct regimes: with few components all parameters converge, with more only one converges while the rest diverge, yet loss still decays polynomially.
layout: 2x2 grid of line plots; columns compare M=4 vs M=6; top norms, bottom log-log loss
description: A 2x2 grid of matplotlib line plots with gridlines and sub-captions (a)-(d). The left column is M=4 and the right column is M=6. The top row plots parameter norms ||mu_i|| against iteration, up to 20000, with five colored curves (blue, orange, green, red, purple) and a legend. In (a), all norms drop from 4 and settle near zero, with a brief dip and rebound in one curve. In (b), the norms start at 6, one curve (blue) collapses to near zero, and the other four rise together to about 7. The bottom row shows log(loss) against log(iteration). In (c) the loss falls smoothly to about -5. In (d) the loss has a plateau-like bend and a noisy decline to about -4. The contrast between the top-row panels draws the eye first.
caption: Experimental results illustrating two convergence behaviors. (a, c) For $M=4$, all parameters converge to the ground truth, consistent with [ref]. (b, d) For $M=6$, only one parameter converges while the others diverge, consistent with [ref]. The loss curve in (d) exhibits a convergence rate close to $O(1/\tau)$ in the final phase.
abstract: Score matching has become a central training objective in modern generative modeling, particularly in diffusion models, where it is used to learn high-dimensional data distributions through the estimation of score functions. Despite its empirical success, the theoretical understanding of the optimization behavior of score matching, particularly in over-parameterized regimes, remains limited. In this work, we study gradient descent for training over-parameterized models to learn a single Gaussian distribution. Specifically, we use a student model with $n$ learnable parameters and train it on data generated from a single ground-truth Gaussian using the population score matching objective. We analyze the optimization dynamics under multiple regimes. When the noise scale is sufficiently large, we prove a global convergence result for gradient descent. In the low-noise regime, we identify the existence of a stationary point, highlighting the difficulty of proving global convergence in this case. Nevertheless, we show convergence under certain initialization conditions: when the parameters are initialized to be exponentially small, gradient descent ensures convergence of all parameters to the ground truth. We further prove that without the exponentially small initialization, the parameters may not converge to the ground truth. Finally, we consider the case where parameters are randomly initialized from a Gaussian distribution far from the ground truth. We prove that, with high probability, only one parameter converges while the others diverge, yet the loss still converges to zero with a $1/Ï$ rate, where $Ï$ is the number of iterations. We also establish a nearly matching lower bound on the convergence rate in this regime. This is the first work to establish global convergence guarantees for Gaussian mixtures with at least three components under the score matching framework.
